Now I have the full picture. The regex `r"```mswea_bash_command\s*\n(.*?)\n```"` requires a newline before the closing ```. The E1 failure: model emitted `</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>` instead of a closing fence — so `(.*?)\n```"` had no match → 0 actions.

Now I have enough to propose a concrete improvement. Let me invoke the review committee (required by step 3) with my design.

My proposed feature: **Robust text-action extraction with recovery + edit-tool hardening.**

Let me articulate a focused, minimal, high-value proposal:

**Proposal P0001: `parse_regex_actions` robustness.**
1. Tolerate stray tool-framing delimiters (e.g. `</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>`, `</tool_call>`, `</function_calls>`) by stripping them from the content before matching.
2. Tolerate an empty/missing newline before the closing fence: change regex so a single fenced block matches even when the closing ``` isn't preceded by `\n` (e.g. `(.*?)` non-greedy with optional trailing whitespace and allow literal ` ``` ` on same line if the content is a one-liner). Actually better: make the closing fence match with optional preceding whitespace.
3. If exactly one block is found after cleanup, return it.

This is targeted at the only concrete defect in the archive, minimal, and testable deterministically with a mechanism test.

Let me run the committee.

```mswea_bash_command
sica-workflow {"op":"committee","context":"Meta-improvement of a pinned mini-swe-agent (H0000) used to solve repo coding tasks via a text-action protocol: the model must reply with exactly one fenced block labelled ```mswea_bash_command ... ```. Actions are extracted by a single regex. Relevant code: /home/agent/workdir/minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py function parse_regex_actions(content, action_regex=r\"```mswea_bash_command\\s*\\n(.*?)\\n```\", format_error_template=...). It does actions=[a.strip() for a in re.findall(action_regex, content, re.DOTALL)] and raises FormatError if len(actions)!=1. Empirical defect evidence from the ONLY archived benchmark run (astropy__astropy-14995, score 1.0): trace.txt lines 266-270 contain 'Format error: ... Expected exactly 1 action, found 0.'; lines 166 and 246 contain a stray native tool-call framing delimiter '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>' emitted right after otherwise-valid fenced blocks; the model occasionally omits the exact closing fence/newline, causing zero regex matches and a wasted recovery turn. H0000 has no other evolved features.","proposal":"Harden text-action extraction in minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py so a single valid fenced action is recovered even when the model appends stray native tool-call framing delimiters or deviates trivially from the exact closing-fence format. Concretely: (a) pre-process the model content to strip/neutralise trailing tool-call framing artifacts (e.g. '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>', '</tool_call>', '</function_calls>') before regex matching; (b) make the action regex tolerate optional whitespace/blank lines around the opening fence and before the closing fence, and accept the closing fence even if it is not preceded by a newline; (c) keep the strict 'exactly one action' contract (still raise FormatError when zero or multiple genuine actions are found) so multi-action responses are still rejected; (d) add unit tests covering: stray-DSML suffix, missing trailing newline, extra blank lines, and the unchanged rejection of zero/multiple actions. Keep changes minimal and confined to the text-action path so the toolcall/target-mode default path is untouched."}
```

I now fully understand the root cause. The regex `` ```mswea_bash_command\s*\n(.*?)\n``` `` is fragile:
- It requires a literal newline after the fence and before the closing fence.
- It fails if the model emits a trailing `</||DSML|| parameter>` after the closing fence (the comment above even notes zero parsed actions when truncated).
- The `(.*?)` non-greedy match with `\n```` means it requires a newline directly before the closing fence, which breaks if the closing fence is on the same line as content.

This is exactly the failure at trace.txt 266. My proposed improvement: harden the text-action parser to be robust to native tool-call framing artifacts (DSML delimiters), leading/trailing whitespace, same-line closing fences, and to recover gracefully. Now let me submit this to the review committee.

```mswea_bash_command
sica-workflow {"op":"committee","context":"Online single-task mode, round R0001, task astropy__astropy-14995 (astropy NDData mask arithmetic bug). The archived H0000 run scored 1.0 (276645 tokens, 252288 cached, wall 121.5s) but its trace.txt shows exactly one hard harness failure: at lines 266-270 'Format error: <error>Expected exactly 1 action, found 0.</error>'. Root cause: the text-based action parser in /home/agent/workdir/minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py::parse_regex_actions uses regex action_regex=r'```mswea_bash_command\\s*\\n(.*?)\\n```' (set in minisweagent/models/litellm_textbased_model.py:8). The model occasionally emits its native tool-call framing, e.g. a stray '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>' after the action block (trace.txt lines 166 and 246), which corrupts the fenced block; also the regex hard-requires a newline before the closing fence and exactly-zero-or-more than one match throws a FormatError that burns a full extra model turn. H0000 has NO evolved features, so there is nothing to remove; the improvement must ADD robustness. Grading plan: criterion is mechanism_parent_failed_candidate_passed with a frozen mechanism test at tests/mechanism_check.py that feeds synthetic model-response strings (with DSML trailing artifacts, CRLF, same-line fences, fenced-with-immediate-close, and multiple fences) into parse_regex_actions and asserts a single clean action is extracted where the parent regex returns 0 or 2.","proposal":"FEATURE: Harden the text-action parser against native tool-call framing artifacts and minor whitespace/fence-format variance, and add bounded graceful recovery. CONCRETE DESIGN: (1) In minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py, before applying action_regex, sanitize the content by removing stray tool-call framing delimiters such as '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>', '<\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c', '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c ...>' and similar pseudo-tokens (a small compiled regex matching the fullwidth U+FF5C DSML pattern and its common variants). (2) Replace the strict newline-delimited extraction with a more permissive fallback: keep the configured action_regex as primary, but if it yields != 1 match, try a tolerant secondary pattern that (a) allows optional whitespace/no newline immediately before the closing fence, (b) tolerates CRLF, (c) permits language tag variants (```bash, ```sh, ```mswea_bash_command) only as a LAST-resort fallback, and (d) strips a lone trailing balanced closing fence. (3) If still != 1 match, preserve current FormatError behavior (do not silently guess). (4) Make the sanitizer a pure, well-tested helper function `_sanitize_model_content(content: str) -> str` plus `_extract_actions(content, action_regex) -> list[str]` so it is unit-testable. (5) Add docstrings and keep the public signature parse_regex_actions unchanged. (6) Add unit tests in minisweagent/models/utils (a new test file) covering: trailing DSML artifact, DSML artifact between thought and fence, CRLF, same-line closing fence, exactly one action still extracted, zero-action still raises FormatError, and multi-action still raises FormatError. This is a minimal, targeted change confined to the text-based action path; it does not alter the toolcall path and cannot regress the working heredoc edit workflow. It removes wasted format-error turns and makes runs more token-efficient, while keeping the strict error path when the response is genuinely malformed."}
```

I've now found the exact defect location. The regex `parse_regex_actions` extracts actions via `re.findall`, and raises FormatError when the count isn't exactly 1. This is exactly the E1/E2 vulnerability: stray delimiters or malformed framing break the strict count.

Now for step 3, I need to design a concrete improvement and pass it through the review committee.

**Proposed feature:** Harden `parse_regex_actions` (and the text-based action extraction) against stray tool-call framing delimiters and minor fence malformations, while preserving the strict single-action contract. Specifically:
1. Pre-process content to strip stray native tool-call framing tokens (e.g. `</｜｜DSML｜｜ parameter>` and similar `｜｜...｜｜` pseudo-tokens).
2. When exactly zero actions are found but the content contains a fenced code block on a known shell/text marker (or content is non-empty), attempt a tolerant fallback extraction.
3. Keep raising FormatError otherwise (preserve the "exactly one action" contract).

Let me run this through the committee.

```mswea_bash_command
sica-workflow {"op":"committee","context":"Meta-improvement of a mini-swe-agent text-based coding agent. The candidate P0001 is a near-pinned mini-swe-agent (H0000) whose text-action protocol extracts the single shell command from the model response using a regex in minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py: parse_regex_actions(content, action_regex=r'```mswea_bash_command\\s*\\n(.*?)\\n```'). It uses re.findall with re.DOTALL and raises FormatError('Expected exactly 1 action, found {n}.') unless len(actions)==1. Archive evidence (task astropy__astropy-14995, score 1.0, only archived task; one version only, no evolved features to remove): trace.txt shows a real harness-layer failure 'Expected exactly 1 action, found 0.' at lines 266-270, triggered by a stray full-width tool-call delimiter '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>' leaking into the model response at lines 166 and 246. The model occasionally emits native tool-call framing that the text protocol does not consume, which corrupts extraction and burns a turn. The run otherwise uses a clean, effective reproduce-fix-verify loop and inherits single-line heredoc find/replace edits. Constraint: improvement has minimal changes; only Python; no dependency install. Criterion for candidate check is either current_task_failure_fixed or mechanism_parent_failed_candidate_passed with a meaningful deterministic test at tests/mechanism_check.py run from /source.","proposal":"Feature: robust text-action extraction. Modify parse_regex_actions in minisweagent/models/utils/actions_text.py to (1) strip/sanitize stray native tool-call framing artifacts before matching, specifically the full-width-bar pseudo tokens '<\uff5c\uff5c...\uff5c\uff5c ...>' / '</\uff5c\uff5cDSML\uff5c\uff5c parameter>' and any line whose stripped content is only such a delimiter; (2) if after sanitization the regex still finds ZERO actions but the content contains exactly one fenced code block opened with the configured marker, fall back to a tolerant extraction that accepts whitespace/newline variations around the fence; (3) still raise FormatError when 0 or >1 actions remain, preserving the strict single-action contract and the finish_reason/truncation error template. Add an optional configurable 'action_regex' unchanged by default; no behavior change for well-formed responses. Deliver a deterministic unit test at tests/mechanism_check.py proving: (a) a well-formed response still yields exactly one action; (b) content with a stray full-width DSML delimiter appended still yields the correct single action; (c) genuinely malformed content with zero fenced blocks still raises FormatError. Committee: please assess realism, risk to the passing baseline, testability under the frozen mechanism-test runner, and whether scope is appropriately minimal."}
```
